title: Correlation IDs
description: Learn to use correlation IDs to trace requests across microservices.

data.text: Correlation IDs are unique identifiers that link all logs, traces, and events for a single request across multiple services. Netflix, Amazon, and Google all use correlation IDs extensively to debug distributed systems.

A correlation ID is a unique identifier generated at the entry point of a request (API Gateway, load balancer, or first service). It is passed through all services via HTTP headers and included in every log entry, trace span, and event.

data.title: Correlation ID Flow
items: Client sends request (optionally with X-Correlation-ID header)
API Gateway generates correlation ID if not present
Gateway passes correlation ID in X-Correlation-ID header to backend
Each service extracts correlation ID from the header
Each service includes correlation ID in all logs and traces
Each service passes correlation ID to downstream calls

data.title: W3C Trace Context
data.text: The W3C Trace Context specification defines traceparent and tracestate headers for propagating correlation IDs. Adopt this standard for interoperability with OpenTelemetry and other tools.

data.title: Example: Correlation ID in HTTP Headers
data.content: Pass correlation ID through HTTP headers across services.
data.code:
# Client -> API Gateway
GET /api/orders/123
X-Correlation-ID: req-abc123

# API Gateway -> Order Service
GET /orders/123
X-Correlation-ID: req-abc123
X-Span-ID: span-456

# Order Service -> Payment Service
POST /payments
X-Correlation-ID: req-abc123
X-Span-ID: span-789

# Every log entry includes the correlation ID:
# {
#   "correlationId": "req-abc123",
#   "message": "Processing payment for order 123"
# }

data.caption: Correlation ID propagation across services
data.definition:

    G -->|X-Correlation-ID: req-abc| O[Order Service]

items.question: Should the client or server generate the correlation ID?
items.answer: Preferably the server (API Gateway) generates it if not present. This ensures consistency. Accept client-provided IDs for end-to-end tracking from mobile apps.

items.question: What is the difference between correlation ID and trace ID?
items.answer: In OpenTelemetry, the trace ID is the correlation ID. They serve the same purpose: linking all telemetry for a single request.

items.question: How do I search logs by correlation ID?
items.answer: Index correlation IDs in your log aggregation tool (Elasticsearch, Loki). Use Kibana or Grafana to search for all logs with a specific correlation ID.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Correlation IDs link telemetry across services
Generate at the entry point, propagate via headers
Include in every log, trace, and event
Use W3C Trace Context for standardization
data.takeaway: Correlation IDs are essential for debugging distributed systems; implement them in every service.
